dish.title: Ghanaian Red-Red: Black-Eyed Pea Stew with Spiced Roasted Plantains

recipe_version.title: Ghanaian Red-Red: Black-Eyed Pea Stew with Spiced Roasted Plantains
recipe_version.description: Black-eyed peas simmered in a vivid red stew of red palm oil, tomato, onion, ginger, garlic, and Scotch bonnet, served with oven-roasted ripe plantains tossed in ginger and cayenne (a baked take on kelewele).

steps.title: Preheat and prep
steps.body: Turn the oven on to 425 F to preheat and line a sheet pan with parchment. Dice the onion, mince the garlic, grate the ginger, and drain the peas. Peel and chunk the plantains and toss them with the oil, 1/2 tbsp ginger, the cayenne, and 1/2 tsp salt.

steps.title: Roast the plantains
steps.body: Spread the plantains on the pan and roast in the preheated 425 F oven 25 to 28 minutes, flipping once, until caramelized at the edges. Runs inside steps 3 to 5 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Build the stew base
steps.body: Warm the red palm oil in the Dutch oven over medium. Cook the onion until soft, 5 minutes; add the remaining ginger and the garlic for 1 minute, then the tomato paste for 1 minute, stirring.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.body: Add the crushed tomatoes, 1 cup water, the Scotch bonnet, and 1 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer 10 minutes, then add the peas and simmer 10 minutes more, stirring now and then and mashing a few peas to thicken.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Remove the Scotch bonnet. Serve the red-red in bowls with the roasted plantains alongside.
